answer: One concrete Sybil defense is slashable staking: each agent locks a non-transferable bond (an economic quill) before it may sign an attestation or draw a reward. Minting fake keys is cheap, but activating each one is not — an attacker needs N separate locked bonds for N Sybils, and any coordinated echo of votes exposes the shared funding and forfeits every bond. Because the reward per verified identity is capped, the cost to the attacker rises linearly with the size of the fake nebula while the payoff per node stays flat, so past a small threshold the attack becomes unprofitable.
